notes: freq_band_low_hz/freq_band_high_hz are derived from reference-recording acoustics and should transfer across deployments. onset_threshold_factor reflects the source recordings' own background noise, not any particular property's field SNR -- treat it as a starting point and re-validate against real pulled TDOA attempts before trusting it long-term. See tools/README.md.

Bush Stone Curlew.notes: Derived 2026-07-25 from 152 calls across 5 unique Xeno-canto samples (7 downloaded, 2 exact-duplicate files dropped: XC589420, XC597375) via tools/derive_species_bands.py's automated energy-envelope call segmentation + derive_band (5-95th percentile cumulative spectral energy, 150Hz margin). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls (not a single median) to cover the real spread of call content rather than collapsing to one point -- see tools/derive_species_bands.py's module docstring for why a discrete-cluster approach was tried first and rejected. onset_threshold_factor left at the 8.0 factory default -- not derived from these reference recordings, needs empirical validation against real pulled TDOA attempts on this property.

Gray Butcherbird.notes: Reprocessed 2026-07-25 (supersedes the 2026-07-13 hand-derived value) using tools/derive_species_bands.py: 139 calls scored across 7 unique Xeno-canto samples (8 downloaded, XC640428 dropped as a content-duplicate of XC635936 -- confirmed via duration + fingerprint match, same underlying recording re-listed under a different catalog number, matching the prior manual finding). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls, wider than the 2026-07-13 tight-cluster value on both edges -- an earlier attempt this session tried splitting calls into discrete high/low clusters and taking a union of cluster medians, but the underlying distribution turned out to be a smooth continuum with no real gap, so a percentile range was used instead (see tools/derive_species_bands.py's aggregate_species() docstring). onset_threshold_factor (6.0) unchanged -- this pass only re-derives the band, not the onset threshold.

Laughing Kookaburra.notes: Derived 2026-07-25 from 29 calls across 7 Xeno-canto samples (2 of the 7 files scored zero calls -- too quiet for the segmentation threshold used, not further investigated) via tools/derive_species_bands.py's automated energy-envelope call segmentation + derive_band (5-95th percentile cumulative spectral energy, 150Hz margin). Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls. Lower call count than other species in this batch -- treat this band with somewhat less confidence than the others derived the same day; worth adding more reference recordings if this species proves to be a common trigger source. onset_threshold_factor left at the 8.0 factory default -- not derived from these reference recordings, needs empirical validation against real pulled TDOA attempts on this property.

Noisy Miner.notes: Reprocessed 2026-07-25 (second pass, same day as the initial 6-species batch) using tools/derive_species_bands.py. The initial run used the same call-segmentation --threshold-factor (6.0) as every other species and scored only 26 calls, with 3 of 7 source files scoring zero -- too quiet for that threshold. Rerunning with --threshold-factor 3.0 recovered signal from 2 of those 3 (XC60735, XC60739) but pushed the proposed band even higher (1237-17905Hz), not lower. Per-file inspection found the real cause: XC837694 alone contributed 51 of 93 scored segments at that threshold, with a consistently extreme high edge (median 16667Hz, max 19339Hz) at regular ~0.5-0.7s intervals across the whole ~40s clip -- a pattern consistent with a continuous insect/cicada chorus rather than sparse bird calls, not confirmed by ear. Excluding XC837694 (done ad-hoc for this run, not yet a reusable --exclude-files option in tools/derive_species_bands.py -- see project memory) while keeping --threshold-factor 3.0 gives 724-9369Hz off the remaining 42 calls across 6 files, rounded to 720-9370. Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz, same method as every other species. Note the call-segmentation threshold-factor used to derive this band (3.0) differs from every other species processed this way (6.0) -- that's a tuning parameter of the derivation script only, unrelated to onset_threshold_factor below (which governs real-time onset detection on the hub, not band derivation). onset_threshold_factor (5.0) left unchanged from the 2026-07-13 value -- this pass only re-derives the band. Still wider than most other species in this file; worth re-validating against real pulled TDOA attempts on this property before trusting long-term.

Pied Currawong.notes: Reprocessed 2026-07-25 (supersedes the 2026-07-13 hand-derived value) using tools/derive_species_bands.py: 91 calls scored across 8 unique Xeno-canto samples (10 downloaded, 2 exact-duplicate files dropped: XC604355, XC831892). The automated segmenter's noise-floor filter (drops any segment whose derived low edge lands at/near derive_band()'s own 50Hz floor -- i.e. no defined tonal content) independently reproduced the prior manual exclusion of XC580877 as a likely wind/rustle-contaminated outlier, without needing to hardcode it. Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls. onset_threshold_factor (5.5) unchanged -- this pass only re-derives the band.

Scaly-breasted Lorikeet.notes: Derived 2026-07-25 from 56 calls across 6 Xeno-canto samples via tools/derive_species_bands.py's automated energy-envelope call segmentation + derive_band (5-95th percentile cumulative spectral energy, 150Hz margin), same --threshold-factor (6.0) as the main 2026-07-25 batch. Band = 10th percentile low_hz to 90th percentile high_hz across all scored calls. Widest band of any species in this file, but checked per-file before applying: no single recording dominates or looks contaminated (per-file high_hz medians spread smoothly ~4200-11900Hz across all 6 source files, largest single-file sample n=19) -- treated as real call variation, not noise, consistent with lorikeets' harsh broadband calls. onset_threshold_factor left at the 8.0 factory default -- not derived from these reference recordings, needs empirical validation against real pulled TDOA attempts on this property.
